messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a spike of noisy alerts this morning from console when teams set percentile thresholds. Looks like the percentile calc is being done over tenant-aggregated streams instead of per-route. :eyes: Link: https://redwood.console/alerts/XXX (screenshot attached)
maria: Oof. Which config field is the rule using? `percentile_window` or the older `threshold.type=percentile`?
alex: It's the new percentile rule. Repro config snippet:

```
{
  \"threshold\": {
    \"type\": \"percentile\",
    \"percentile\": 95,
    \"window_secs\": 300,
    \"aggregation\": \"tenant\"   // default from console today
  }
}
```

When aggregation is `tenant` we combine routes and the 95th ends up dominated by a few hot routes so tiny routes get flagged constantly.
darren: That sounds like an API vs UX mismatch. For percentile thresholds we should default to `per_entity` (per-route) unless the user explicitly wants cross-route aggregation. Changing default is breaking though.
jess: Related ops concern: switching to per-route will change alert volume and maybe cost/telemetry cardinality. We need a rollout that checks ingestion cardinality impact and account quotas.
maria: On the console side we can make the scope explicit in the rule editor — radio: [per-route] [service-wide] with a hover explaining impact. That should reduce accidental tenant-wide percentiles.
alex: Agreed. Quick ask: can we stop the current tenant-agg rules from firing while we fix? Some customers are paged repeatedly.
darren: Short-term mitigation: add a noise-suppressor for percentile rules with low-traffic entities (min_samples threshold). Quick API tweak: `min_samples: 10` to ignore tiny routes.
jess: That buys time. For the longer fix I propose:
- feature flag that flips default aggregation for percentile rules to `per_entity`
- canary to 10% tenants for 48h
- telemetry retention for the experiment at 30d and a backfill job optional for customers

maria: I'll own the editor copy & UX. I'll add a warning when switching aggregation and a small explainer modal.
alex: Any concerns about notify/routing policies? Will escalation rules behave differently if we split alerts by route vs aggregated alerts?
darren: Yes — escalation and dedupe logic assumes one fingerprint per rule. If we split by route we must update fingerprinting to include `route_id`. We also need to adapt alert buckets for oncall quotas so one noisy tenant doesn't exhaust notify budget.
jess: Good catch. Add to rollout checklist: update fingerprint schema, adjust per-entity notify quotas, and monitor page rate per-oncall for the canary group.
deploy-bot: deploy started: api/alerts-service@fix-percentile-agg (canary)
deploy-bot: deploy success: api/alerts-service@fix-percentile-agg -> canary :tada:
maria: PR opened for console changes: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-console/pull/4823 — added scope selector + warning modal. Will add tests and screenshots.
darren: API PR for default flip + `min_samples` field: https://github.com/redwood/alerts-service/pull/1298 — also adds `fingerprint.route_id` path. cc @jess for quota changes.
jess: I'll add quota schema updates and a telemetry dashboard: "percentile-agg-canary" with: alert-rate, pages-per-oncall, cardinality-by-tenant. Will wire alerts for unexpected notify budget burn.
alex: Thanks team — sounds like a plan. Can we have a brief sync after the canary (tomorrow 10am PT) to decide global flip? :thumbsup?
maria: ✅ I'll schedule and add notes to the rollout doc.
darren: I'll monitor the canary logs and put a slack alert in #eng-oncall if anything spikes.
(reacts: alex :thumbsup: on maria message)
